features.headline: Commanders running low on time to 'put it all together'
features.desc: Dan Quinn knows it's repetitive to say the Commanders are close, but now they're painted into a corner.
body: LANDOVER, Md. — Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels didn't hesitate. After yet another loss, and after falling three games under.500, Daniels — and his teammates — know that their season is slipping away.
So, when asked Sunday night if he worried they had enough time to turn it around, he quickly replied, "Yeah. Next week is a must-win."
Earlier, teammate K'Lavon Chaisson said, "Yeah, damn right" when asked a similar question.
Unfortunately for the Commanders, it's a familiar place. But it's also indicative of their season. At 2-5-1, they're three games behind the New York Giants (5-2-1) in the NFC East.

Mathematically the Commanders remain alive, but with nine games remaining, any realistic hope the team has for a strong finish likely begins and ends vs. the Giants on Thursday (8:15 p.m. ET, Prime Video).
A win and they would be two games back with eight to play and own the tiebreaker — if that eventually mattered.
"We all know how badly we need this," Washington coach Dan Quinn said. "Everyone in this building understands that."

Another loss would drop them to 7-18-1 since the start of last season and likely intensify the speculation by analysts over Quinn's future. Owner Josh Harris has not publicly commented on Quinn's job. Quinn said he regularly meets with Harris before and after games and also on Mondays.
But in training camp, one team source said what has been repeated by others at various points: "It's a results business."

And the results need to improve. Washington has now played five one-score games; the Commanders are 1-3-1 in those games — and 3-7-1 since the start of 2025. In 2024, when they went 12-5, Washington was 8-4 in one-score games — but that included a four-game winning streak at season's end.

features.headline: Seven things Solak thinks for NFL Week 10: Jaguars trades, All-Pro picks, more
features.desc: Get ready for Week 10 with takes on the Jaguars winning the AFC, Shedeur Sanders not earning a starting role, Fred Warner being the best player in football and more.
body: Are you excited for NFL Week 10? With nine weeks in the history books and nine more weeks to go, I can't remember a season with as dense a top tier of NFL contenders. Nobody feels immortal, but many teams feel mighty.

We're gonna learn a lot in Week 10 — the Patriots against the Lions in Munich, the Vikings in Green Bay for a critical divisional rematch, and the Steelers at the Bengals on Sunday night — and a lot more in the weeks to come. November should be fun.
Every Tuesday of the NFL season, I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions.

They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out.
And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.
This week, I'll start by lauding the Jaguars for going all-in on the trade deadline Monday, play some deadline bingo and then cast my votes for a midseason All-Pro team.

Jump to: Jaguars are AFC favorites? Quiet trade deadline on the horizon? Who makes the midseason All-Pro team? Sanders isn't good enough to unseat Watson? Could Lock be a bridge QB in 2027? Warner is the best football player? Vikings need to trade for a QB? Some extra inklings

Monday was Jaguars day in the NFL, as second-year general manager James Gladstone made three trades during the day. He sent a 2027 second-rounder and 2028 fifth-rounder to Atlanta for safety Jessie Bates III.

features.headline: As Jaylen Brown faces the Celtics for the first time, familiar questions linger
features.desc: Jaylen Brown and the Philadelphia 76ers host Jayson Tatum and the Boston Celtics on Tuesday night.
body: FOR MUCH OF his decade-long career with the Boston Celtics, Jaylen Brown spent time answering questions about his role.
Critics wondered whether he and Jayson Tatum could coexist, speculated about whose team it was. Both players, their teammates and coaches were aware of the narrative.
"The media wants to kind of sometimes write the story that pulls us apart," Brown said in 2021. "But we talk a lot. We don't let it bother us."
So as Brown — now a Philadelphia 76er after Boston traded him this offseason — sat at Sixers media day a month ago, a reporter asked him: "Do you guys know who the alpha is?"
There were years of frustration loaded into Brown's smirk and two-word response: "Next question."
Four months into his Sixers tenure, Brown has again fielded questions about his relationship with his former running mate in Boston, partly because of a social media firestorm Brown started.
It has led to back-and-forth comments between Brown and Tatum, and a report from NBC Sports and Celtics TV analyst Brian Scalabrine about Brown's "demands" and "trade request" in Boston.
Scalabrine later walked back his comments about Brown asking for a trade.
A source with knowledge of the situation told ESPN that there was no truth to the report.
Instead, the source said, Brown discovered his former team had tried — and failed — to trade him to the Milwaukee Bucks while he was on vacation over the summer.
The one thing Brown did ask for, the source said, was to be involved in the process of where he was traded. The Celtics ignored the request and sent him 300 miles southwest to Philadelphia.

features.headline: The historic (and absurd) longevity of Steph Curry and Kevin Durant
features.desc: More than 10 years after briefly joining forces, Steph and KD remain near the top of their games at 38. How long can each legend keep this up?
body: When Stephen Curry and Kevin Durant teamed up a decade ago, their union created perhaps the most lethal scoring duo in NBA history and threatened to serve as the foundation of a dynasty that might have rivaled Michael Jordan's Chicago Bulls.
Curry and Durant were both former MVPs and scoring champions in their primes at 28 years old when they began their first title chase together in 2016-17.
As the Golden State Warriors raced out to a 20-3 start that fall, they were so thoroughly dominant that critics quickly deemed the pairing "unfair."

There have been two key developments since those halcyon early days: The Curry and Durant partnership disbanded quicker than anyone could have expected, while Curry and Durant (both now 38) have managed to sustain elite play much longer than anyone anticipated.

The first point is well-worn. After two championships and a torn Achilles, the nomadic Durant left the Bay Area to start fresh with the Brooklyn Nets. Meanwhile, Curry has become one of the NBA's all-time single-franchise icons.

The second point has been obscured by LeBron James' record-setting longevity. As James has rewritten the record books and kept playing into his 40s, Curry and Durant have prospered late in their respective careers like few superstars before them.

With Curry's Warriors and Durant's Houston Rockets set to face off Wednesday for the first time this season (9:30 p.m. ET, ESPN) let's take a moment to appreciate their remarkable staying power a full decade after they started torching the league as teammates.

features.headline: Breaking down the CFP race for three conferences after Week 10
features.desc: The margin between winning the conference and making the CFP is considerably wider for certain teams.
body: We're entering Week 11 of the college football season, and yet, somehow less time means more questions. Nobody seems to know what to do with the Heisman, and I'm not seeing a price worth chasing right now.
For the record, Notre Dame QB CJ Carr (+220), Miami QB Darian Mensah (+250) and Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith (+280) are the three favorites.
The national title board hasn't moved enough to change my mind, either. So, let's look elsewhere.
Who will make the playoff? Who will win their conference? Between the remaining schedules and tiebreakers, there's plenty to sort through before we put money on any of it.

I went into the MAC thinking 7-2 Ohio might be the play. The Bobcats are undefeated in conference play, host Toledo (7-2 overall, 4-1 MAC) in Week 13 and boom: +295 to win it. There's something there.
But then I looked at how those teams match up, and Toledo's defense kept getting in the way. Ohio wants to run. Toledo is really good at stopping it, and it also has a much better passing game.
So now I'm looking at Ohio's bigger payout and asking whether I actually like the matchup or just the number.

Toledo at +146 isn't exactly giving us some huge discount. Western Michigan (6-3, 4-1 MAC) has a manageable schedule left, but I don't trust its offense as much. I can make a case for all three getting to the championship game. I'm less interested in paying these prices to find out which one does.

Memphis (7-2, 4-1 AAC) was the team I kept looking at in the American. I like Marcus Stokes and the passing game. I trust the Tigers' pass defense more than North Texas' or UTSA's. But Memphis still has to go to South Florida and Navy.

features.headline: Cooper Flagg breaks down in-game peanut butter and jelly sandwich
features.desc: Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg has recently started eating an in-game peanut butter and jelly sandwich.
body: With a comfortable lead against the Brooklyn Nets on Sunday, Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg headed to the bench for good early in the fourth quarter. He put on his warmups, sat next to teammate Daniel Gafford and watched the Mavericks close out a 130-93 victory.
Moments later, the Mavericks' TV broadcast caught Flagg with a small plastic bag in hand, taking out a peanut butter and jelly sandwich and having a bite.
"Boy, that looks good right now," former Mavericks guard Derek Harper said on the broadcast.
It marked the second consecutive game Flagg enjoyed a peanut butter and jelly sandwich during the action.

Last Friday, his in-game meal came during a 112-100 win over the Utah Jazz in which he racked up 21 points, 10 rebounds, seven assists and three steals. Cameras similarly spotted him taking a bite. Flagg followed that up with 25 points, a career-high 12 assists and five rebounds in Sunday's game.

Not surprisingly, reporters asked the second-year forward about his in-game snack. He first nodded to the Mavs' strength and medical staff before clarifying that he's trying to put on weight and gain muscle.

"So those requirements I got to meet. I'm just trying to stay ahead of it," Flagg said Sunday. "We got another game [Monday]. So just trying to get my calories and stay ahead of it and be ready for another one [Monday]."
Flagg said that he prefers smooth peanut butter and grape jelly. He added that he also enjoys sandwiches with peanut butter and banana, while sometimes adding honey.
